answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because copper only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, island is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any meadow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
